title: Descent of the actual compact-support projection mate along completion
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $O$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On each small pro-etale site put $A_{n,T}=(O/\ell^n)_T$ and $R_T=\varprojlim_n A_{n,T}$, identified with the pulled-back integral coefficient sheaf [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x]. Write $r_TN=(N\otimes^L_{R_T}A_{n,T})_n$ for derived reduction [det-sp-reduction-tower-normalized], and $L_T=R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_n$ for total derived inverse limit of strict towers after restriction of scalars to $R_T$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. All derived categories are ordinary unbounded module derived categories; tower operations are the simultaneous section-model operations of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], with exact evaluations [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian].

Use the normalized descent-map presentation [def-sp-complete-projection-descent-maps]. Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$ and let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting] with compactification $c=(j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X,p:\bar X\to Y)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Put $F_R=Rp_{*,R}j_{!,R}$, $F_\bullet=Rp_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}$, and use ordinary derived module pullback and tensor [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek]. Let $M\in D(R_X)$ and $K\in D(R_Y)$ be derived complete with bounded-below reduction towers. Put $U=F_R(M\otimes^Lf_R^*K)$ and $V=(F_RM)\otimes^LK$. Assume $M\otimes^Lf_R^*K,U,V$ are derived complete with bounded-below reduction towers. Assume the canonical compactification/limit comparisons identify $F_RN$ with $L_YF_\bullet r_XN$ and the canonical reconstruction counits identify $r_YF_RN$ with $F_\bullet r_XN$, for $N=M$ and $N=M\otimes^Lf_R^*K$; comparisons and augmentations here have the strict-diagram normalization of total derived limit, not chosen level isomorphisms.

Let $\theta:F_\bullet(r_XM)\otimes^Lr_YK\to F_\bullet(r_XM\otimes^Lf_\bullet^*r_YK)$ be the proper counit projection mate followed by the inverse open unit projection mate on these systems. Suppose both system projection mates are invertible. The canonical tensor/scalar and pullback/scalar comparisons and the specified reconstruction counits identify its source with $r_YV$ and its target with $r_YU$ as derived systems. Write $\widetilde\theta:r_YV\to r_YU$ for this composite.

The ordinary integral compact-support projection transformation $\pi_R:V\to U$, formed from the same proper counit and inverse open unit projection mates, satisfies the equality of derived morphisms
$$\pi_R=\eta_U^{-1}\circ L_Y(\widetilde\theta)\circ\eta_V.$$
This equality is natural in $M,K$ and is normalized by those actual units, counits and quotient augmentations. Consequently $\pi_R$ is invertible, with inverse obtained by replacing $\widetilde\theta$ by $\widetilde\theta^{-1}$ in this formula. No monoidality of $L_Y$, faithfulness of level evaluations, or finite-field hypothesis on $k$ is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sp-complete-projection-reduction-square]. The target coordinate is invertible by the reconstruction hypothesis and the specified tensor/scalar and pullback/scalar isomorphisms. Postcompose the square with its inverse to obtain r_Y(pi_R)=transportedProjection.

Use the actual composed reduction/limit adjunction. The unit of the normalized completed reduction adjunction is invertible on complete U and V by [det-sp-normalized-equivalence]. The other unit factor belongs to the derived strict-tower equivalence, so it and its image under total limit are invertible. Adjunction.comp_unit_app therefore makes the actual units eta_U and eta_V invertible.

The proper projection and inverse open projection are invertible by hypothesis. Functors preserve their isomorphisms and the pullback compositor, so the transported projection is invertible. Unit naturality gives pi_R;eta_U=eta_V;L(r_Y(pi_R)). Substitute the first step and postcompose eta_U inverse. Define the requested integral isomorphism as eta_V, L of the transported system isomorphism, eta_U inverse. Its hom and inverse have exactly the asserted formulas.

Uncurry the proper counit tensor projection natural transformation to get its two-variable naturality square. Paste the naturality of the integral open projection and the pullback compositor; tensor functoriality and pushforward functoriality give the requested naturality equation for the actual compact-support projection.

old_proof.text: For each $T$ let $q_T:(T^{\mathbf N},A_{\bullet,T})\to(T,R_T)$ be the ringed sequence projection. By [lem-coef-sequence-projection-derived-adjunction] its derived pullback is exactly $r_T$, computed by the one strict quotient complex of a flat-term K-flat representative. By [lem-coef-sequence-pushforward-limit-projections], $Rq_{T*}=L_T$ with the prescribed total-limit projections. Thus $r_T\dashv L_T$ has actual unit $\eta$ and counit $e$ with the normalization in the question. The ringed sequence sites and their operations are those of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Use $\mu:r(A\otimes^LB)\cong rA\otimes^LrB$ and $\nu_u:rLu_R^*\cong Lu_\bullet^*r$ from [lem-sp-reduction-derived-monoidal-tower]. Their compatibility with quotient augmentations fixes all the tensor and pullback coordinates used below.

old_proof.text:
Put $Z=\bar X$. For the commutative square with vertical edges $p:Z\to Y$, $p_\bullet:Z^{\mathbf N}\to Y^{\mathbf N}$ and horizontal edges $q_Z,q_Y$, let $h_B:r_YRp_{*,R}B\to Rp_{*,\bullet}r_ZB$ be the mate of the canonical pullback square. In particular $h_B$ is the transpose under $Lp_\bullet^*\dashv Rp_{*,\bullet}$ of $r_Z$ of the proper counit, after $\nu_p$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] to this square, with arbitrary $B\in D(R_Z)$ and $K\in D(R_Y)$. It gives
$$Rp_{*,\bullet}(a^p_{B,K})h_{B\otimes^LLp_R^*K}\,r_Y(\pi^p_R)=\pi^p_\bullet(h_B\otimes1)\mu_{Rp_{*,R}B,K},$$
where $a^p=(1\otimes\nu_p)\mu$. This is an equality in the derived category of systems, for the counit-defined projections $\pi^p$; the cited theorem allows arbitrary ringed topoi and arbitrary structural ring maps. No invertibility of $h$ or $\pi^p$ is used here.

old_proof.text:
Let $d_N:r_Zj_{!,R}N\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{!,\bullet}r_XN$ be the canonical open scalar comparison. The localized ringed-site and ringed-diagram assertions of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] apply to the constant sequence ring $\Delta R_Z\to A_{\bullet,Z}$ and its restriction to $X$. On quotient representatives $d$ is $[x]\otimes a\mapsto[x\otimes a|_X]$. It carries the open unit to the system open unit: after restriction both sides are $x\otimes a\mapsto x\otimes a$. This identity is simultaneous in the quotient diagram by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]; the scalar tensor and restriction comparisons are $\mu,\nu$ of Step 1.

Write $\gamma_R:j_!N\otimes^LJ\to j_!(N\otimes^Lj^*J)$ and $\gamma_\bullet$ for the inverse-unit open projection maps. Their inverses are the open adjuncts of unit tensor identity by [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Taking these adjuncts, the two routes in
$$j_{!,\bullet}(a^j_{N,J})\,d_{N\otimes^Lj^*J}\,r_Z(\gamma_R)=\gamma_\bullet(d_N\otimes1)\mu_{j_!N,J}$$
restrict to the same unit tensor identity, by the displayed formula for $d$ and the unit-compatible $\mu,\nu$. The open adjunction Hom bijection therefore gives the equality before evaluating the systems. Here $a^j=(1\otimes\nu_j)\mu$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), compatibility of the inverse open unit projection with reduction

old_proof.text:
For $N=M,H:=M\otimes^Lf_R^*K$, denote the assumed compactification/limit isomorphism by $\alpha_N:F_RN\to L_YF_\bullet r_XN$. Its reconstruction transpose is
$$b_N=e_{F_\bullet r_XN}\,r_Y(\alpha_N):r_YF_RN\xrightarrow{\sim}F_\bullet r_XN.$$
We check which comparison this is. The assumed normalization writes $\alpha_N$ as $Rp_{*,R}j_{!,R}(\eta_N)$ followed by the open/limit and proper/limit comparisons and scalar restrictions. The proper/limit comparison is the direct-image composition comparison for $pq_Z=q_Yp_\bullet$; by [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] that composition comparison is adjunction-compatible. Its conjugate is the proper mate $h$ in Step 2. The open/limit comparison is conjugate to $d$ in Step 3: its transpose is the open scalar map whose restriction is the same open unit, hence equals $d$ by the open adjunction Hom bijection. Pasting these squares by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], and cancelling $L_X(e)\eta_{L_X}=1$ and $e_{r_X}r_X(\eta)=1$, gives
$$b_N=Rp_{*,\bullet}(d_N)\,h_{j_{!,R}N}.$$
These cancellations use the actual reduction/limit adjunction of Step 1. Thus this is the comparison specified in the question, not an identification inferred only from finite projections.

source.place: Paragraphs (2)-(3), normalization by the compactification/limit comparisons and reconstruction counits

old_proof.text:
Apply Step 2 with $B=j_{!,R}M$ and Step 3 with $N=M$, $J=Lp_R^*K$, using $j^*Lp_R^*K\cong Lf_R^*K$. The canonical pullback-composition comparisons are monoidal and adjunction-compatible by [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons], so $a^j,a^p$ combine to the specified scalar tensor/pullback identification for $H$. Compose the proper equality with $Rp_{*,\bullet}$ of the open equality. Naturality of $h$ moves $\gamma_R$ past $h$; Step 4 then identifies each $Rp_{*,\bullet}(d_N)h_{j_!N}$ with $b_N$. The result is
$$b_H\,r_Y(\pi_R)=\theta\,(b_M\otimes1)\mu_{F_RM,K},$$
with the input tensor/pullback coordinates understood. By definition, conjugating the right side by these same coordinates and $b_H$ is $\widetilde\theta:r_YV\to r_YU$. Hence $r_Y(\pi_R)=\widetilde\theta$. This uses equalities of whole-system transformations from Steps 2-4, without detecting equality by finite evaluations.

source.place: Paragraph (3), pasting the proper and open factor identities

old_proof.text: Naturality of the actual unit of $r_Y\dashv L_Y$ gives $\eta_U\pi_R=L_Y(r_Y\pi_R)\eta_V$. The units $\eta_U,\eta_V$ are invertible: $U,V\in D(R_Y)$ are derived complete [sk-def-pe-derived-completion], so their canonical maps to the derived limits of their uniformizer reductions are isomorphisms, and transporting the Roos triangle of that limit along this isomorphism makes the canonical map the first map of a Roos triangle, which is derived completeness in the sense of [def-weil-derived-complete]. Apply [det-sp-normalized-equivalence] with $T=Y$: $\ell$ is invertible on $Y$ since $p\ne\ell$, its coefficient sheaf is our $R_Y$, its functors are the same $r_Y$ and $L_Y$, and it handles the cofinality of the powers of $\ell$ and of the uniformizer. Its unit $M\to L_Yr_YM$ is invertible on derived-complete objects. Two adjunctions with the same functors $r_Y\dashv L_Y$ have units differing by a natural automorphism of $L_Yr_Y$, so the actual unit $\eta$ of Step 1 is invertible at $U$ and $V$ as well. Substituting Step 5 and multiplying by $\eta_U^{-1}$ proves the asserted formula. Both system projection mates are invertible by hypothesis, and all coordinate comparisons are isomorphisms, so $\widetilde\theta$ is invertible. Functoriality shows that $\eta_V^{-1}L_Y(\widetilde\theta^{-1})\eta_U$ composes with the asserted map in both orders to the identity. All the squares used above are natural in both inputs; inversion of a natural family of isomorphisms is natural. This proves the stated naturality and normalization, using neither monoidality of $L_Y$ nor any restriction on $k$ beyond the stated hypotheses.
